title: Studying the organ and leading a group at Count Basie's bar
summary: After the Apollo dates he studied organ for three years, then led a group with Percy France and Danny Farrar at Count Basie's bar in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Mostly original. '20th Century Blues,' which I considered to be my contribution to the modern ranging and composing which was going on during that time, which was comparable to Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker's thing, even though it was different. But what happened, after I made these recordings I went to California and I studied the organ because the organ was becoming popular then and I had heard Fats Waller play it in Tulsa, Oklahoma earlier, way when I was young.

And so I got interested in the organ, and I studied the organ for about three years, and I went back to New York and formed a group and played in Count Basie's bar. And from there I went to Europe with Buck --
Who did you have in that group, can you remember?

I had a saxophone player by the name of Percy France, a genius player, very wonderful player. And I had a drummer by the name of Danny Farrar, spelled F-a-r-r-a-r. He later went with Jonah Jones for awhile, good drummer, played with good feeling. And that was very exciting experience. And from there I had the pleasure of going to Europe with Buck Clayton and his fine group.
